description: Building Atlas, the AI film-production platform at an early-stage AI startup. I designed and built two of its production modules on my own (Slate and Storyboard) and shipped performance, AI and reliability upgrades to its timeline video editor.
highlights: Owned features end to end: PostgreSQL schema and Alembic migrations, FastAPI services, background jobs, React UI and deploy scripts
Integrated AI providers (fal.ai, OpenAI) behind fallbacks and job queues, so generation failures surface as clear, retryable states instead of silent errors

modules.name: Slate
modules.summary: A Frame.io-style workspace where film teams organise projects, review cuts frame by frame, leave feedback in context and move work through approval, built from an empty folder to a full product.
highlights: Two-tier role-based access: workspace roles (Owner / Admin / Editor / Viewer) mapped onto project roles (Owner / Editor / Reviewer / Viewer), with private projects and per-stage visibility resolved in one place
Frame-accurate video review with SMPTE and frame timecodes, plus an FFmpeg rendition ladder (1080p / 720p / 480p, never upscaled) generated by background jobs with retry
Threaded, timecoded comments with @mentions, on-frame annotations (pin, arrow, rectangle, freehand, text) and voice, screen or screen + camera recordings as attachments
Version stacks with an approval workflow (Needs Review → Needs Changes → Approved), activity log, notifications, calendar, workload board and a command palette
Public share links protected with PBKDF2-hashed passwords, expiry and download controls; email invites that report delivery failures instead of hiding them
Storyboard boards with AI-generated frames and Script AI, PDF and spreadsheet export, and in-browser PSD and PDF previews, covered by 14 Vitest suites

modules.name: Storyboard Studio
modules.summary: Turns a script into sequences of shots, generates frames with AI, and cuts them into a timed animatic with voice, music and SFX that exports to MP4 straight from the browser.
highlights: Project → Sequence → Shot system with shot editing, annotations, version history, grid / table / single views and CSV / JSON round-trip import and export
Multi-track animatic timeline with transitions, snapping, an SFX library, clipboard, drag-to-trim and in-browser voice-over recording
Browser-side MP4 export using WebCodecs (VideoEncoder / AudioEncoder) and mp4-muxer, with an OfflineAudioContext mixdown and a MediaRecorder fallback
AI Frame Studio: batch shot generation via fal.ai with a curated Draft / Standard / Pro model matrix, style presets and continuity-aware prompts
Audio AI pipeline (per-shot TTS from shot context, dialogue, music and lip-sync) plus Script AI on fal any-llm with automatic OpenAI fallback
Story bible and reusable characters, backgrounds and props that shots reference for consistent generation; background jobs panel with live ETAs; shot media history with a radial revision picker

modules.name: Timeline Editor
modules.tagline: Enhancements to the NLE-style video editor
modules.summary: Contributed AI, audio, performance and reliability features to Atlas's multi-track video editor.
highlights: AI gap-fill: GPT-4o Vision reads the frames on both sides of a timeline gap and writes the prompt that bridges them, with frames routed through a media proxy (blob cache, in-flight de-duplication) to get around R2 CORS
Real audio waveform extraction and Premiere-style audio detachment, with clip speed applied to both video and detached audio

Cut timeline cold-load time by removing duplicate API calls, splitting track and asset fetches, decoding waveforms server-side and adding a list cache and payload normalisation, all with pytest coverage
Upload queue manager with concurrency limits, real XHR progress and pause / resume / cancel / retry, bound to React via useSyncExternalStore
Fixed program-monitor playback stutter and a dirty-state bug that marked successful cloud saves as unsaved; added a live save-status indicator
